text:
incident-bot: Paging: p99/router latency spike detected affecting streaming responses across us-west and eu-west regions. auto-page to #oncall, #infra, #runtime. severity: sev2 :rotating_light:

sara (oncall): on it. seeing alerts for p95 and p99. which service?

javier (infra): router frontends show tail latency jump starting ~1805000800. heatmap: lots of requests hitting warm-fallback pool. looks like the fallback policy accidentally prefers warm nodes when route table misses.

sara (oncall): is that the new policy rollout from last night?

javier (infra): yes — policy-change: fallback_strategy=warm_prefer rolled out to 50% at 1804997000. quick grep of logs:

```
# /var/log/router/frontend.log | grep fallback_count | tail -n 5
[1805000941] route=gen-ctx user=svc-alpha fallback=warm pool=warm-01 fallback_count=48 rt=3600ms
[1805000955] route=chat user=svc-beta fallback=warm pool=warm-03 fallback_count=52 rt=4200ms
[1805001012] route=embed user=svc-gamma fallback=warm pool=warm-02 fallback_count=60 rt=4800ms
```

javier (infra): warm pool nodes are CPU-bound and exhibit higher latency for long streaming sessions. fallback selection is causing hot partitions.

tess (support): I'm seeing customer reports: some streaming sessions time out around 5s, a handful of webhook retries from enterprise customers. ticket count up ~12 in last 20m.

mike (runtime): streaming stalls correlate with concurrent KV-cache miss + fallback hops. Warm nodes don't have full KV caches for recent prefixes. That causes repeated remote cache fetches — increases head and tail latency.

sara (oncall): impact: p95 went from ~220ms to 950ms, p99 up to 4.8s for the last 30m. Not total outage but user-visible degradation for streaming and some long generations.

yusuf (sre): recommended immediate mitigation: flip fallback_strategy to cold_prefer for routed models and throttle warm pool acceptance. We can also temporarily increase route timeouts to reduce error churn.

javier (infra): I can patch the routing policy flag. proposing a 2-step: 1) set fallback_strategy=cold_prefer globally for routed paths 2) mark warm pools as drainable for new sessions (no new sessions to warm-*)

sara (oncall): do it. communicate to support so they can update customers.

javier (infra): applying patch now -> `curl -XPOST https://console.internal.api/routing/flags -d '{"fallback_strategy":"cold_prefer"}'`

deploy-bot: Rolling change: routing/flags update started by javier at 1805001137. 3/3 control-plane nodes ack.

javier (infra): change accepted. pushing drain marker to warm pools: `kubectl label nodes pool=warm-01 evict=true` (done)

mike (runtime): draining warm pools. initiating graceful session migration rules and reducing admission window to avoid burst cutover.

yusuf (sre): also bumping router concurrency limit from 256 -> 320 on frontends in us-west to absorb in-flight connections while warm pool drains.

sara (oncall): support note: "We applied a routing configuration rollback to prefer cold pools and are draining a small warm pool. We're seeing improvements but monitoring closely. We'll follow up if any customer needs a manual remediation."

tess (support): posted to affected customers list, sent update to the enterprise queue.

# 7 minutes later

javier (infra): metrics: p95 dropped to ~310ms, p99 to ~600ms in us-west after flip. eu-west slightly lagging due to control plane propagation.

mike (runtime): streaming stalls reduced; KV miss rate on frontends down ~70%. Still seeing a few stragglers where sessions initiated on warm nodes earlier keep stalling. We're expiring stale session allocations in 5m windows.

sara (oncall): handoff: I need to go offline in 25m. mike — please take next oncall for the incident. yusuf + javier will be backup for infra changes.

mike (runtime): taking it. notes: watch p99, K/V-remote fetch latency, and any error spikes in webhook retries. I'll keep chat updates every 10m.

javier (infra): follow-up action items captured: [1] revert fallback_strategy after we validate telemetry (if stable) [2] audit policy rollout pipeline to add canary checks for pool cache fullness [3] add alarm: fallback_count increase > 10/min triggers preemptive rollback

yusuf (sre): also adding a short-term metric: per-pool kv-cache-hitrate (new gauge) so we can gate fallback decisions.

sara (oncall): customer impact summary for postmortem: "Root cause: policy rollout caused routing to prefer warm fallback pool which lacked hot prefix caches, producing cache-miss amplification and increasing tail latency for streaming. Impact: degraded p95/p99 for streaming generation calls across multiple regions; ~12 customer tickets, no data loss, some requests retried/timeout. Mitigation: rolled back fallback preference, drained warm pool, increased router concurrency, and added monitoring/alerts."

# final check

mike (runtime): p99 trending <700ms globally. KV-cache-miss queue drained. I'll keep an eye and close once stable for 1h.

sara (oncall): thanks team. documenting timeline in incidents/ and will open a postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident update: severity downgraded to sev3 at 1805001299; page cleared.
